newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia shares close higher as gold shines at last.
newsitem.headline: Australia shares close higher as gold shines at last.

text.p: Australian shares closed on a strong tone on Tuesday as gold stocks moved higher for the first time in four days and yield-sensitive stocks rose on hopes of another interest rate cut.
The All Ordinaries index was 16.9 points up at 2,696.1, just off the intra-day high of 2,697.0.
Market turnover topped over A$1.04 billion (US$773 million), with trade boosted by Rupert Murdoch's News Corp's A$325 million sale of its entire stake in magazine group PMP Communications.
The rise in the broader market ended four days of falls following the sale of the majority of the gold reserves of the Reserve Bank of Australia.
Brokers said the market could continue to make up the recent lost ground on Thursday if Wall Street hits the 8,000 level, the Dow industrials closed at 7962 points on Tuesday.
Australia's battered gold sector was the strongest riser on Wednesday up over three percent. The index had lost 16 percent over the four days to Tuesday.

Banks and insurance stocks also performed well as investors took heart from 10-year bond futures contracts near three and a half year lows. The short-term yield has already factored in another interest rate cut.
The insurance index closed over two percent up, while banks ended over one percent higher. The Reserve Bank last cut official cash rates by 0.5 percentage points to 5.5 percent.
Investors are tipping a further cut soon and June jobs data on Thursday may be the trigger. Employment is expected to rise over 40,000 for the month of June after falling by a similar amount in May.
"If there is a bad number tomorrow there could be another rate cut," said Robert Osborn, an analyst at fund managers Tyndall Australia.
